title: Fitting Room Six
hook: I close a clothing store at the mall. One rule: if a fitting room is locked after the lights go out... don't look under the door.
lines: I close a clothing store at the mall. Alone. Every night.
My manager gave me one rule. After the mall lights go out, if a fitting room is locked... don't look under the door.
Just knock twice, say "we're closed," and walk away.
For a whole year, every door swung open empty.
Then one night, right after the big lights shut off, fitting room six was locked.
"We're closed." No answer. No breathing. Just the hum of the lights... and my own heartbeat.
Instead, I got down on the cold floor... and looked under the door.
White sneakers. Scuffed toes. One red lace... exactly like mine.
Then the lock clicked... and the door swung slowly open.
The room was empty. Just the tall mirror... and me, kneeling in it.
I looked down. I was kneeling there in my socks.
And out in the dark mall... I heard my own footsteps, walking toward the exit.
